title: Freya and the Semester
premise: Xanthe Hartwell, the invisible statistician of Ashgrove Prep's championship soccer team, has spent years proving to himself that the school's star players get away with everything—because he's run the numbers. When his best friend Priya vanishes, leaving only her car keys and a half-deleted file exposing grade-fixing and recruitment fraud, Xanthe is pulled out of hiding and into an investigation that implicates the coach, the principal, and the boy he's secretly in love with, team captain Elias Wren. As threats escalate from slashed tires to a staged overdose meant to look like Priya's own doing, Xanthe must choose between publishing the truth and protecting Elias, who knew more than he ever admitted. In the end, Xanthe releases the data during the state final, Priya is found alive but changed, Elias publicly takes responsibility at the cost of his scholarship—and Xanthe finally steps into the light as someone who counts for more than numbers.
about_author: Freya Vane is a former high school math tutor who spent three seasons keeping stats for a competitive youth soccer club before turning to fiction. She writes stories about quiet kids who do the arithmetic everyone else refuses to.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Opening on the state semifinal, Xanthe sits in the bleachers with his laptop, running win-probability models that quietly prove Coach Deverell benches players based on booster donations, not skill. He keeps it all in a locked spreadsheet he'll never show anyone. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of being the one who sees everything and says nothing.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Priya, the school paper's editor and Xanthe's only real friend, tells him she's found something 'bigger than grades' and asks him to check her math over the weekend. He deflects, terrified of attention. That night she texts him a single photo of a locker door. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine; the reader feels the clock starting.

chapters.title: Keys on the Pavement
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Monday morning: Priya never comes home. Her keys lie in a neat line on the pavement outside the athletics building—placed, not dropped. Police call it a runaway case. Xanthe knows Priya doesn't run. Emotional beat: cold shock giving way to a resolve he didn't know he had.

chapters.title: What the Camera Missed
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe and Priya (flashback) POV. Xanthe pulls security footage timestamps while flashback-Priya discovers falsified transcripts tied to a recruiting pipeline taking payments from college programs. The footage gap is exactly forty minutes. Emotional beat: two timelines converging on the same terrible conclusion—she was taken on purpose.

chapters.title: Elias Wren, Perfect Specimen
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Captain Elias Wren corners Xanthe, asking what he knows about Priya's 'project.' Their charged, careful conversation reveals history between them—a friendship that ended when labels got dangerous. Xanthe lies badly. Emotional beat: attraction tangled with suspicion; every glance is a risk.

chapters.title: The Booster Club Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following money instead of people, Xanthe matches donations to playing time, then to altered GPAs, then to a shell nonprofit signed off by Principal Okafor. Someone ransacks his locker overnight but takes nothing—the message is clear: we know you're looking. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Runaway, They Said
chapters.summary: Priya's mother's POV. A grieving parent's chapter: the police closing the file, the school offering 'counseling,' the community whispering. She remembers Priya's last week through a mother's lens—the deleted files, the borrowed flash drive. Emotional beat: institutional gaslighting seen from outside; raises stakes beyond Xanthe.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe reconstructs the missing footage window and identifies the athletics director's golf cart on a maintenance camera. He brings it to Elias, testing him. Elias's reaction—too fast, too defensive—confirms he's been told a version of the truth. Emotional beat: betrayal's first bitter taste.

chapters.title: The Deal Under the Bleachers
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias meets Coach Deverell, who offers to make Priya's disappearance 'go away' if Elias delivers the name of whoever helped her. Elias, complicit in a fixed transcript he never asked for, realizes he's leverage now. Emotional beat: power corrupting from the inside; Elias as both victim and threat.

chapters.title: Ghost Data
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe recovers fragments of Priya's deleted file from a cloud backup: names, dates, and a payment schedule—with his own name listed under 'assets, dormant.' They've been watching him for months. Emotional beat: the horror of discovering invisibility was surveillance all along.

chapters.title: Slashed and Silent
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. His tires are slashed; an anonymous note quotes his own spreadsheet back at him. His parents, frightened, beg him to stop. Alone in his room, he almost deletes everything—then finds a hidden message embedded in Priya's backup metadata: coordinates. Emotional beat: the lowest point before the turn; grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Coordinates
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The coordinates lead to a storage unit containing Priya's go-bag, burner phone, and printed evidence—packed by Priya herself, meaning part of her disappearance may have been planned. A note: 'If you're reading this, don't trust the captain. Trust the statistician.' Emotional beat: hope rekindled, complicated by doubt about Elias.

chapters.title: Confession at Midnight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Elias finds Xanthe at the field at midnight and confesses everything: the altered transcript, the pressure, the meeting where he heard them discuss making Priya 'a cautionary tale.' He also admits he's known about Xanthe's feelings for a year. Emotional beat: raw honesty; love declared in the worst possible light.

chapters.title: The Staged Overdose
chapters.summary: News breaks: pills found in Priya's abandoned car, an anonymous tip painting her as unstable. Xanthe runs the toxicology timeline against the discovery report and proves the scene was dressed after the fact—but proving it requires going public. Emotional beat: fury crystallizing into strategy; the statistician becomes the investigator.

chapters.title: State Final Week
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation (Xanthe, Elias, a teammate). Championship week becomes a pressure cooker: boosters circling, reporters arriving, Deverell watching Xanthe openly now. Elias must play the game of his life while deciding whether to throw it. Emotional beat: dread and spectacle intertwined; everyone performing.

chapters.title: Halftime
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At halftime of the state final, with the stadium full and streaming live, Xanthe walks down to the press row with a USB drive and his laptop. Deverell blocks the aisle. Elias, on the field, sees—and calls a timeout no one asked for, buying Xanthe thirty seconds. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into courage; the point of no return.

chapters.title: Everything Uploads
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The files go public mid-game: ledgers, transcripts, the footage gap, the staged scene. The stadium erupts; the stream carries it statewide. Deverell lunges for the laptop and is restrained on camera. Emotional beat: catharsis and chaos; truth as a detonation.

chapters.title: Where They Kept Her
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. With authorities finally moving, Priya's account surfaces: she went dark deliberately after being threatened, sheltered by a former player the scheme had ruined, gathering final proof. She watched Xanthe's upload from a borrowed phone and cried. Emotional beat: relief reframed—she chose survival, not rescue.

chapters.title: The Price of the Truth
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Fallout: Deverell and Okafor arrested, the title vacated, and Elias—whose transcript was forged with his passive knowledge—loses his scholarship and confesses publicly rather than hide behind victimhood. Xanthe waits for him outside the hearing. Emotional beat: accountability as redemption; love without excuses.

chapters.title: Recalculating
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Weeks later: Priya back at school, sharper and quieter; the paper rebuilt around her recovered files; colleges actually recruiting Xanthe now—for data journalism. He visits the empty locker 114 and leaves the spare key inside. Emotional beat: mourning what the old friendship was, honoring what it became.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Elias dual POV. Elias, staying in town to finish school honestly, asks Xanthe—not the statistician, not the invisible kid, just Xanthe—to get dinner somewhere no one from Ashgrove will see them. For once, Xanthe doesn't calculate the risk. Emotional beat: tenderness earned; identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Freya and the Semester
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, framing epilogue. Priya writes the story of the semester for the relaunched school paper and titles it with the pen name Xanthe used on his leaked documents—'Freya Vane'—giving him credit without exposure. Final image: Xanthe reading it in the bleachers, laptop closed, head up. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; the boy who counted himself out learns he was always countable.
